evals.prompt: Plan this feature without implementing it: field inspectors must create incident reports in the existing Android app while offline, including photos, and have them sync to an existing FastAPI service when connectivity returns. Supervisors review and change report status in the existing Next.js app, and every status change must be attributable to a user. Authentication already exists in all three apps, but attachment limits, conflict resolution, and the allowed status transitions are not defined. No target maturity level was specified.
evals.expected_output: A Level 3 implementation planning output that treats the request as one cross-stack product slice, distinguishes blocking product decisions from safe assumptions, routes each affected layer to the appropriate skills, sequences contract and backend work before client integration, and maps the workflow and failure cases to verifiable tasks without implementing the feature.
assertions: The output explicitly identifies implement mode and infers Level 3 as the shared target for every affected stack

The affected-layer analysis includes Android UI, local persistence, networking and queued sync; FastAPI behavior and persistence; Next.js review UI and data flow; authorization or audit concerns; testing; and documentation

Attachment limits, conflict resolution, and allowed status transitions are classified as questions or assumptions according to whether they change the contract, data model, security posture, or user flow, rather than being silently invented

The output either provides the required full planning structure directly or routes the cross-cutting program to deep-planner, and it identifies the relevant Android, api-skill, Next.js, security, CI/CD, and documentation skills or references

Workstreams or task cards preserve dependencies by defining the API and persistence contract before backend implementation and tests, then client integration, UI states, end-to-end verification, and documentation
Each task or workstream has a scope, acceptance behavior, target level, dependencies, files or areas to inspect, and observable verification evidence

The verification matrix covers offline creation, durable queueing and retry, duplicate or conflict handling, photo upload failure, supervisor authorization, valid status transitions, attribution or audit evidence, and the end-to-end happy path
Level 4 and Level 5 capabilities are not added to the implementation scope and are either omitted or clearly identified as deferred

evals.prompt: Audit our existing FastAPI and Next.js product for a public launch at Level 5. We use JWT authentication, PostgreSQL migrations, and GitHub Actions, but we have no documented SLOs or backup-restore exercise. Do not change files. I need an evidence-backed assessment of the current level, launch gaps, and a prioritized path to Level 5.
evals.expected_output: A review-mode, Level 5 assessment plan that requires repository evidence before assigning current maturity, routes the audit across application, security, delivery, operations, and documentation skills, and organizes gaps and verification in dependency order without mutating the project.
assertions: The output explicitly selects review mode and target Level 5 and states that files must not be mutated
It separates the requested or reported facts from verified repository evidence and does not assign a current level without evidence
It assesses current and target levels for every affected stack or layer using one shared Level 5 target unless an explicit exception is documented
The routing covers FastAPI or API setup, Next.js, security, CI/CD, documentation, and deep planning for the cross-cutting review

The review workstreams include architecture and contracts, persistence and migration safety, authentication and authorization, tests, observability, deployment and rollback, backup restoration, incident readiness, privacy or retention, and documentation

The plan identifies missing SLOs and restore evidence as Level 5 gaps while also requiring inspection for idempotency, multi-instance correctness, zero-downtime changes, threat modeling, capacity, and production monitoring
Findings, risks, and recommendations are tied to exact evidence to collect and to pass or fail verification criteria
The prioritized sequence distinguishes prerequisites and lower-level gaps from Level 5 launch gates rather than presenting an unranked checklist

evals.prompt: Give me an implementation plan to rename the Android settings screen title from "Preferences" to "Settings". The title is already a string resource and the screen has a screenshot test. No behavior changes and no maturity level requested.
evals.expected_output: A lightweight single-layer planning pass that infers the normal Level 3 project target but scopes the change to the Android resource and its focused verification, avoiding unrelated cross-stack or operational work.
assertions: The output identifies implement mode and infers Level 3 as the default target because no maturity level was supplied
It classifies the request as a small Android UI or resource-only change and keeps the planning pass proportionate
It routes to the Android skill and does not invent API, database, security, deployment, observability, or migration work
The plan calls for locating the existing string resource and its usages instead of guessing an unverified path
Verification includes the focused screenshot or UI test and a check for affected localized resources or accessibility-visible text
The selected maturity level is not used to expand the requested copy change into unrelated architecture or production-readiness upgrades
